artworks.title: Heraclitus
artworks.credit: Gift of B. Asscher, Amsterdam and H. Koetser, Amsterdam.
artworks.caption: A seventeenth-century portrayal of Heraclitus.
artworks.description: Ter Brugghen’s imagined Heraclitus leans on a terrestrial globe. The painting forms a pair with his Democritus.
artworks.alt: Heraclitus as imagined by Hendrick ter Brugghen: an older man resting his head on one hand, leaning on a globe.

artworks.title: Democritus
artworks.credit: Gift of B. Asscher, Amsterdam and H. Koetser, Amsterdam.
artworks.caption: A seventeenth-century portrayal of Democritus.
artworks.description: Ter Brugghen’s laughing Democritus rests his arm on a celestial globe. The painting forms a pair with his Heraclitus.
artworks.alt: Democritus as imagined by Hendrick ter Brugghen: a laughing man in a beret, leaning on a celestial globe.

artworks.title: Portrait of Pythagoras
artworks.credit: Purchased with the support of the F.G. Waller-Fonds.
artworks.caption: Pythagoras, imagined in a Renaissance engraving.
artworks.description: An imagined portrait from a series of Greek and Roman philosophers and writers.
artworks.alt: A Renaissance engraving of Pythagoras as a bearded man wearing a cap, with his name beneath the portrait.

artworks.title: Studies for the Death of Empedocles
artworks.museum: SMK – National Gallery of Denmark, Copenhagen
artworks.caption: Rosa’s study of the legend of Empedocles at Etna.
artworks.description: A sequence of figures depicts the legendary leap into Etna. This is an illustration of the story, not evidence of how Empedocles died.
artworks.alt: Salvator Rosa’s pen-and-ink studies of falling figures for the legend of Empedocles at Etna.
